```text
160	export const clipToMask = (
161	  context: CanvasRenderingContext2D,
162	  mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement,
163	  offsetX: number,
164	  offsetY: number,
165	) => {
166	  const cx = mask.x + mask.width / 2 + offsetX;
167	  const cy = mask.y + mask.height / 2 + offsetY;
168
169	  context.translate(cx, cy);
170	  context.rotate(mask.angle);
171	  context.translate(-mask.width / 2, -mask.height / 2);
172
173	  context.beginPath();
174	  const outline = getMaskOutline(mask);
175	  if (outline.type === "rect") {
176	    if (outline.radius && context.roundRect) {
177	      context.roundRect(0, 0, outline.width, outline.height, outline.radius);
178	    } else {
179	      context.rect(0, 0, outline.width, outline.height);
180	    }
181	  } else if (outline.type === "ellipse") {
182	    context.ellipse(
183	      outline.width / 2,
184	      outline.height / 2,
185	      outline.width / 2,
186	      outline.height / 2,
187	      0,
188	      0,
189	      Math.PI * 2,
190	    );
191	  } else {
192	    outline.points.forEach(([x, y], index) =>
193	      index ? context.lineTo(x, y) : context.moveTo(x, y),
194	    );
195	    context.closePath();
196	  }
197	  context.clip();

199	  context.translate(mask.width / 2, mask.height / 2);

205	export const getMaskSvgPathData = (mask: ExcalidrawMaskElement) => {
206	  const outline = getMaskOutline(mask);
207	  if (outline.type === "rect") {
208	    const { width: w, height: h } = outline;
209	    const r = Math.min(outline.radius, w / 2, h / 2);
210	    if (!r) {
211	      return `M0 0H${w}V${h}H0Z`;
212	    }
213	    return (
214	      `M${r} 0H${w - r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${w} ${r}V${h - r}` +
215	      `A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${w - r} ${h}H${r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 0 ${h - r}` +
216	      `V${r}A${r} ${r} 0 0 1 ${r} 0Z`
217	    );
218	  }
219	  if (outline.type === "ellipse") {
220	    const rx = outline.width / 2;
221	    const ry = outline.height / 2;
222	    return (
223	      `M0 ${ry}A${rx} ${ry} 0 1 0 ${outline.width} ${ry}` +
224	      `A${rx} ${ry} 0 1 0 0 ${ry}Z`
225	    );
226	  }
227	  return `${outline.points
228	    .map(([x, y], index) => `${index ? "L" : "M"}${x} ${y}`)
229	    .join("")}Z`;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:06:14Z)**_

I added `"image"` to `MASKABLE_TYPES` in [mask.ts:28-38](packages/element/src/mask.ts#L28-L38). Arrows didn't need a change, because #70 had already made them maskable. I also updated the comment above the set, since it said images were left to #72. I haven't run the tests or the typecheck yet.

Images should be clipped like everything else, because masking works by clipping the canvas (or adding an SVG clip path) around however the element draws. The thing to watch is that image elements have their own crop code, so masked images need checking both on canvas and in export. That fits in with the testing you planned.

I couldn't read the issue for the open question because the `gh` command isn't installed here. Can you paste the "Open Question" section from #72? Once I have it, I'll write up the steps for that part and for the tests.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:22:23Z)**_

Yes, but it was cut on purpose and never built. The original #70 plan let one mask clip many elements: a masking mode where you marked several objects, then a Done button and an "Add elements" button. On 2026-10-21 you cut #70's scope down to **one mask clips one element** and left multiple elements for #72. That decision is in my notes from #70.

The code enforces that limit in three places:

- **[actionMask.tsx:162-174](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx#L162-L174):** `actionApplyMask` applies the mask to the one element you double-click, then leaves masking mode right away.
- **[mask.ts:88-96](packages/element/src/mask.ts#L88-L96):** `canBecomeMask` refuses a shape that already masks something (`!isMaskElement`). So once a mask has a child, you can't re-enter masking mode on it to add another.
- **[mask.ts:58-69](packages/element/src/mask.ts#L58-L69):** `getMaskedElement` returns only the first child it finds. The edit toolbar and the 20% preview use it, so they assume a single child.

The data model already supports many children, because each child stores its own `maskId`. Nothing in the format would need to change. The work is in the parts above: allowing a mask to take more children, re-entering masking mode on an existing mask, and making anything that uses `getMaskedElement` handle a list.

So multiple images (or any mix of elements) under one mask belongs to #72. Is that the open question, or a separate part of the issue?

VS Code's Source Control panel lists untracked files under "Changes" with a **U**, which can look like they're about to be committed. They won't go into a commit unless you stage them.

The only tracked change is [mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts). If you stage just that file (`git add packages/element/src/mask.ts`, or the + next to it in VS Code), your commit will contain only that.

If you want them out of the list, add `.specstory/` to `.git/info/exclude`. That only affects your copy of the repo. Putting it in `.gitignore` instead would hide it for the whole team.

```text
35	  elementsMap: RenderableElementsMap,
36	  allElementsMap: NonDeletedSceneElementsMap,

55	        allElementsMap,
56	        rc,
57	        context,

59	        appState,

61	      );
62	    }
63	  }

68	/**

70	 * outline to `svgRoot` and returns it, so the element can be rendered into it.

72	export const createSvgMaskGroup = (
73	  element: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement,
74	  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
75	  svgRoot: SVGElement,
76	  offsetX: number,
77	  offsetY: number,
78	) => {
79	  const mask = getActiveMaskElement(element, elementsMap);
80	  if (!mask) {

85	  const clipPath = doc.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "clipPath");
86	  clipPath.id = `mask-clipPath-${element.id}`;
87	  clipPath.setAttribute("clipPathUnits", "userSpaceOnUse");
88	  const path = doc.createElementNS(SVG_NS, "path");
89	  path.setAttribute("d", getMaskSvgPathData(mask));
90	  path.setAttribute("transform", getMaskSvgTransform(mask, offsetX, offsetY));

95	  g.setAttribute("clip-path", `url(#${clipPath.id})`);
96	  svgRoot.appendChild(g);
```

I've read through the #70 mask code. The good news is that drawing on canvas, PNG export and SVG export already work one element at a time, so several elements sharing a mask already clip correctly. What needs to change is the masking mode and the checks that assume a mask has only one child.

Here's the plan, based on the original #70 design. I'll do one step at a time and stop after each so you can check it.

1. **Let a mask take more children (logic only).** Replace `getMaskedElement` with `getMaskedElements`, which returns a list, and update `isMaskElement`, `canBecomeMask` and the "remove" case of `actionToggleMask` to use it. Add unit tests in `mask.test.tsx` for one mask with two or more children (including an image), plus remove and release.

   - Check: the typecheck passes and the mask tests pass. Nothing changes in the app yet.

2. **Marking in masking mode.** Add a `markedIds` list to `maskEditor` while picking. Double-clicking an element marks it, and double-clicking a marked element unmarks it. Nothing is applied until you finish. Marked elements get an outline.

   - Check: in the app, mark and unmark several elements and see the outlines.

3. **Done / apply.** Add a Done button to `MaskingModeBar`, styled like Share. Done, or double-clicking empty canvas, applies the mask to every marked element in one undo step. Escape or Cancel throws the marks away.

   - Check: mask two images and a shape together, then undo and redo it.

4. **"Add elements" in the mask toolbar.** This button re-enters masking mode with the mask's current children already marked. Unmarking one and pressing Done releases it from the mask.

   - Check: add an element to an existing mask and remove one from it.

5. **Wrap-up.** Add the new labels to `en.json`, update the tests from #70 that assume clicking once applies the mask straight away, update snapshots, run `yarn fix`, then do a full manual pass including PNG and SVG export.

One change from #70's behaviour: double-clicking empty canvas currently cancels masking mode, and in this plan it would apply the mask instead, like Done. That matches the original #70 design. Does that work, and do you want any other changes before I start step 1?

```text
61	/** the elements clipped by `mask` */
62	export const getMaskedElements = (
63	  mask: ExcalidrawElement,
64	  elementsMap: ElementsMap,
65	): NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] => {
66	  const masked: NonDeletedExcalidrawElement[] = [];
67	  for (const element of elementsMap.values()) {
68	    if (isClippedBy(element, mask)) {
69	      masked.push(element as NonDeletedExcalidrawElement);
70	    }
71	  }
72	  return masked;
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:43:13Z)**_

Step 1 is done. The typecheck passes and all 5 mask test files pass (67 tests).

**Code changes:**

- **[mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts):** `getMaskedElement` is now `getMaskedElements`, which returns every element the mask clips. `isMaskElement` still stops at the first child it finds, so it's no slower.
- **[actionMask.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx):** Ctrl+Alt+G on a mask now releases all its children. Before, it only released the first one it found.

**Tests:**

- **[mask.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/mask.test.tsx):** new tests that a mask finds all its children, that it stops counting as a mask once all of them are deleted, and that a mask already clipping something can take more.
- **[maskActions.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskActions.test.tsx):** new tests that Ctrl+Alt+G on the mask releases both of its two children, and that selecting just one child releases only that one.

Three older tests used an image as the example of something that can't be masked, so they would have failed after the earlier image change. I switched one to a frame and one to an element already clipped by another mask. The third was the eligibility test in [mask.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/mask.test.tsx): images move into the "can be masked" list, and frames and embeds stay as the ones that can't. If you already committed the image change, that commit has these tests failing; this step fixes them.

There's nothing to see in the app yet, because masking mode still applies the mask on the first double-click and exits. Step 2 changes that, so you can mark several elements. Say when to continue.

```js
const sel = h.app.scene.getSelectedElements(h.state);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 18:54:32Z)**_

Step 2 is done. The typecheck passes and all 5 mask test files pass (69 tests). I haven't run the full suite for this step.

**What changed:**

- **[types.ts](packages/excalidraw/types.ts):** while picking, `maskEditor` now has `markedIds`. The `editing` mode has no such field.
- **[actionMask.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx):** masking mode starts with nothing marked. A new `actionToggleMaskMark` marks an element, or unmarks it if it's already marked. It reuses the existing `canBeMasked` check, so the mask itself, other masks, already-masked elements and frames still can't be marked.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):** double-clicking an element in masking mode now marks or unmarks it instead of applying the mask. Double-clicking empty canvas still cancels for now; step 3 turns it into Done.
- **[interactiveScene.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/interactiveScene.ts):** marked elements get a solid blue box outline, the same blue Excalidraw uses for frame highlights. That's separate from the violet selection around the mask. `maskEditor` is now passed to the interactive canvas so it can draw this.
- **Tests:** three tests that compared `maskEditor` now expect `markedIds: []`. The masking mode test that expected a double-click to apply the mask now checks that it marks the element. There are new tests for marking several elements and for unmarking.

**Trying it in the app:** select a shape, press Ctrl+Alt+G, then double-click several elements (images included). Each one should get a blue outline, and double-clicking it again should remove the outline. Escape or Cancel should throw the marks away.

Until step 3 is in, there's no way to actually apply a mask from the app, because nothing applies the marked elements yet. If you commit step 2 on its own, that commit leaves masking broken in the app. The hint in the bar also still says "Double-click an element to mask it"; I'll fix the wording in step 5.

Say when you're ready for step 3.

```typescript
import { actionApplyMask, actionCancelMasking } from "../actions";
import { t } from "../i18n";

import { Button } from "./Button";
import { Island } from "./Island";

import "./live-collaboration/LiveCollaborationTrigger.scss";
import "./MaskingModeBar.scss";

import type { ActionManager } from "../actions/manager";

/** shown at the bottom of the canvas while picking the elements to mask */
export const MaskingModeBar = ({
  actionManager,
}: {
  actionManager: ActionManager;
}) => (
  <Island padding={1} className="masking-mode-bar">
    <span className="masking-mode-bar__hint">{t("labels.mask.picking")}</span>
    <button
      type="button"
      className="masking-mode-bar__cancel"
      data-testid="masking-mode-cancel"
      onClick={() => actionManager.executeAction(actionCancelMasking, "ui")}
    >
      {t("buttons.cancel")}
    </button>
    {/* same look as the Share button */}
    <Button
      className="collab-button"
      data-testid="masking-mode-done"
      style={{ width: "auto" }}
      onSelect={() => actionManager.executeAction(actionApplyMask, "ui")}
    >
      {t("buttons.done")}
    </Button>
  </Island>
);
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 19:08:43Z)**_

Step 3 is done. The typecheck passes and all 5 mask test files pass (75 tests). I haven't run the full suite for this step.

**What changed:**

- **[actionMask.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx):** `actionApplyMask` is now Done. It masks every marked element that can still be masked, in **one undo step**, then selects the mask and leaves masking mode. With nothing marked, it just leaves and records no undo step.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):** double-clicking empty canvas in masking mode now does the same as Done, instead of cancelling.
- **[MaskingModeBar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskingModeBar.tsx):** a Done button next to Cancel, using the Share button's `collab-button` style. The bar imports that stylesheet itself, so it doesn't depend on the Share button being on the page.
- **Tests:** helpers that mark elements and then press Done. New tests cover masking several elements, an unmarked element staying unmasked, Done with nothing marked, undo/redo as one step, the Done button, and Escape or Cancel throwing away marks.

**One thing I hit while testing:** undo didn't revert a test image. It turned out undo ignores images with no `fileId`, even for a plain opacity change, so it's not a masking problem. Real images always have a `fileId`, so the test now gives its image one.

**Trying it in the app:**

1. Select a shape, press Ctrl+Alt+G, double-click two images and a shape, then press Done. All three should be clipped.
2. Do it again, but finish by double-clicking empty canvas.
3. Undo once: all three should come back unmasked together.

Say when you want the full suite run, or go straight to step 4 ("Add elements" in the mask toolbar).

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 19:17:50Z)**_

The basic version is small, about half a step: one helper, one filter, and some tests. That's the same level of support Excalidraw already gives frames.

**How frames do it:** [App.tsx:6625-6640](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L6625-L6640) has a filter in `getElementsAtPosition`: "hitting a frame's element from outside the frame is not considered a hit." That's the only place frame clipping affects interaction.

**The mask version:**

- Add a helper in [mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts), something like `isPointInMask(point, mask)`. Masks are only rectangles, diamonds, ellipses and triangles, so it can reuse the existing `isPointInElement` and outline hit tests from [collision.ts](packages/element/src/collision.ts).
- Add a second filter next to the frame one: an element with an enabled mask only counts as hit if the point is also inside the mask. With clipping switched off, the whole element would be clickable again.

That one filter covers clicking, selecting, hover outlines and the cursor, dragging, double-click to edit text, and double-clicking in masking mode, because they all use `getElementsAtPosition`.

**What it wouldn't cover** (frames don't cover these either):

- **Box and lasso selection:** these use the element's full bounds, so dragging a box over only the hidden part could still select it.
- **Clicking inside an already-selected element:** this uses its full bounding box ([App.tsx:7052-7060](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx#L7052-L7060)), so you could start dragging it from a hidden area.
- **Arrow binding and snapping:** these use their own hit tests in `binding.ts` and the snapping code, so an arrow could still bind to a hidden edge.
- **The selection box and resize handles:** these still surround the whole element.

Closing those gaps would be a step or two more each, and binding is the hardest one.

I'd do the frame-level version: it handles almost everything users click on. If you want it, it fits as a step between 4 and 5, or I can do it right after step 4.

```typescript
import React from "react";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import { GlobalTestState, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

/**
 * mask: filled ellipse at (0, 0)–(100, 100)
 * target: filled rectangle at (50, 50)–(150, 150), clipped by the mask, so
 * its bottom-right corner (e.g. (140, 140)) is hidden
 */
const setup = (maskEnabled = true) => {
  const mask = {
    ...API.createElement({
      type: "ellipse",
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "#a5d8ff",
      fillStyle: "solid",
    }),
    maskEnabled,
  };
  const target = {
    ...API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      x: 50,
      y: 50,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
      fillStyle: "solid",
    }),
    maskId: mask.id,
  };
  API.updateScene({
    elements: [mask, target],
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });
  return { mask, target };
};

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  mouse.reset();
  await render(<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  Object.assign(document, {
    elementFromPoint: () => GlobalTestState.canvas,
  });
});

describe("clicking a masked element", () => {
  it("selects it where it's visible", () => {
    const { target } = setup();

    mouse.clickAt(75, 75);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [target.id]: true });
  });

  it("ignores the parts the mask hides", () => {
    setup();

    mouse.clickAt(140, 140);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
  });

  it("can be clicked anywhere while clipping is off", () => {
    const { target } = setup(false);

    mouse.clickAt(140, 140);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [target.id]: true });
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 19:22:30Z)**_

Both are done. The typecheck passes and all 6 mask test files pass (86 tests). I haven't run the full suite yet.

**Hidden parts can't be clicked (frame-level)**

- **[collision.ts](packages/element/src/collision.ts):** a new `isPointInElementMask` checks whether a point is inside the element's mask, using the mask's shape. Elements with no mask, or with clipping switched off, always pass.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):** a filter in `getElementsAtPosition`, right next to the frame one. Clicking, hovering, dragging and double-clicking now ignore the hidden parts of a masked element.
- **[maskHitTest.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskHitTest.test.tsx)** (new): clicking a visible part selects the element, clicking a hidden part selects nothing, and with clipping off the whole element is clickable again.

**Step 4: "Add elements"**

- **[MaskEditToolbar.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/MaskEditToolbar.tsx):** an "Add elements" button between the Clipping switch and Remove mask. It reopens masking mode with the mask's current children already outlined.
- **[mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts):** `canMarkForMask` allows marking anything that can be masked, plus the mask's own current children. Without that, you couldn't unmark them.
- **[actionMask.tsx](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx):** Done now also releases any children you unmarked, in the same single undo step as the additions. If nothing changed, it just leaves masking mode with no undo step. A brand-new mask still starts with clipping on, but adding elements to an existing mask keeps whatever the Clipping switch was set to.
- **[en.json](packages/excalidraw/locales/en.json):** the new "Add elements" label. The new action is also registered in `actions/types.ts` and `actions/index.ts`.
- **Tests:** 6 action tests and 2 tests that click the toolbar button.

The two parts affect each other: in masking mode, you unmark an existing child by double-clicking its _visible_ part, because its hidden parts can't be clicked anymore.

**Trying it in the app:**

1. Mask an image, double-click the mask twice to open its options, and press Add elements. The image should already be outlined.
2. Double-click a second image to mark it, double-click the first one to unmark it, then press Done. Only the second image should be clipped.
3. Undo once: you should be back to just the first image.
4. Click a hidden part of a masked element: nothing should get selected.

That leaves step 5, the wrap-up. It includes changing the bar's hint, which still says "Double-click an element to mask it". Do you want the full suite run now?

All 6 mask test files pass (86 tests), and the full suite is running in the background. While it runs, here's the full manual check for #72:

**Masking several elements**

- [ ] Select a shape, press Ctrl+Alt+G, double-click two images and an arrow. The bar shows the new hint and each one gets a blue outline.
- [ ] Double-clicking a marked element removes its outline.
- [ ] Done masks all marked elements. Do it again, finishing by double-clicking empty canvas instead.
- [ ] Escape and Cancel throw the marks away and mask nothing.
- [ ] Undo removes the whole mask in one step, and redo brings it back.

**Add elements**

- [ ] Double-click the mask twice to open its options, then press Add elements: the current children are outlined.
- [ ] Mark a new element, unmark an old one, press Done. Undo reverses both in one step.
- [ ] Turn Clipping off, add an element: Clipping stays off.

**Clicking**

- [ ] Clicking a hidden part of a masked element selects nothing, and the visible part still selects it.
- [ ] With Clipping off, the whole element is clickable.

**Removing**

- [ ] Ctrl+Alt+G on the mask releases every child. Ctrl+Alt+G on one child releases only that child.
- [ ] Remove mask in the options releases all children.

**Export**

- [ ] PNG and SVG export with several elements, including images, under one mask: each one is clipped.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:10:33Z)**_

It's a small change, about the size of the hit-test change we just did: one condition and a couple of tests.

The faint preview only shows while the mask is selected (`applyMaskClip` in [maskClip.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/maskClip.ts) checks `selectedElementIds[mask.id]`). The click filter I added in `getElementsAtPosition` could skip the mask check under that same condition. Then a hidden part is clickable exactly when you can see it, and invisible parts stay unclickable.

That also fixes a limitation from step 4. The mask stays selected during masking mode, so the preview shows then too. You'd be able to double-click the faint part of a child to mark or unmark it, not just its visible part.

One thing to decide: clicking a faint part selects that child, which deselects the mask, so the preview disappears. You've grabbed the child, so dragging it still works, but its hidden parts go invisible and unclickable again. Two options:

1. **Keep it as described:** the preview only shows while the mask is selected.
2. **Also show the preview while a child is selected:** after clicking a faint part, that child's hidden parts stay faint and clickable.

I'd do option 1, since it's the smallest and matches how the preview works now. Option 2 is also small, just a wider condition in two places, but it changes the preview behaviour you decided on in #70. Which do you want?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:15:09Z)**_

Option 2 is in. The typecheck passes, all 6 mask test files pass (89 tests), and Prettier reports no formatting issues. I haven't run the full suite yet.

**What changed:**

- **[mask.ts](packages/element/src/mask.ts):** a new `isMaskPreviewShown` decides when the hidden parts are previewed: while the mask **or the element itself** is selected. The drawing and the click test both use it, so the hidden parts are clickable exactly when you can see them faintly.
- **[maskClip.ts](packages/excalidraw/renderer/maskClip.ts):** the 20% preview now also shows while the masked element itself is selected. Exports are still unaffected.
- **[App.tsx](packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx):** the click filter skips the mask check while the preview is showing.

**Tests:**

- **[maskHitTest.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskHitTest.test.tsx):** clicking a faint part while the mask is selected selects the element. A faint part also counts as part of the element while either the element or its mask is selected. With nothing selected, the hidden parts still can't be clicked. To check that last part, the test calls the private `getElementAtPosition`, the same lookup that clicks and hovers use.
- **[maskEditor.test.tsx](packages/excalidraw/tests/maskEditor.test.tsx):** after Add elements, double-clicking a child's faint part unmarks it.

This also removes the step-4 limitation, so in masking mode you can now mark or unmark a child through its faint parts.

**Trying it in the app:**

1. Select a mask: its children's hidden parts show faintly. Click one of those faint parts: that child gets selected, and its faint parts stay visible.

```text
    feat(mask): many-to-many masks that survive grouping and duplication (#74)

    Masks and their elements can now be grouped, transformed, ungrouped and
    duplicated without changing which elements each mask clips.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:30:39Z)**_

I'm stopping here rather than rebasing. #74 overlaps heavily with what we built, and how to combine them is a decision for you (and probably Anthony).

**What #74 changed on master** (Anthony Williams, merged as PR #135):

- **Different data model:** elements now store **`maskIds`**, a list, instead of our single `maskId`. An element can be clipped by several masks at once, and the clips combine so only the overlap shows. Old `maskId` files are converted on load. Every function we touched in `mask.ts` was renamed or changed: `getMaskElement` → `getMaskElements`, `getActiveMaskElement` → `getActiveMaskElements`.
- **It already does part of our #72 work:** one mask clipping several elements, and an add-elements action (`actionAddToMask`) in the mask options. Its masking mode works differently from ours: each double-click applies straight away and you keep going until Escape or a double-click on empty canvas. There's no marking and no Done.
- **It doesn't do images:** its `mask.ts` still says "images are left to #72".

**Conflicts:** 13 of our files were also changed by #74. A plain rebase would conflict throughout `mask.ts`, `actionMask.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `MaskEditToolbar.tsx`, `maskClip.ts` and all the mask tests.

**What only our branch has:**

1. Images can be masked.
2. Hidden parts of masked elements can't be clicked. With several masks, a point would have to be inside **all** of them.
3. Hidden parts can be clicked while the preview shows (mask or element selected).
4. The mark → Done flow, with outlines and the Done button, plus Done releasing unmarked children.
5. The new hint text.

**My recommendation:** keep #74's model, since it's merged and more general. Start a fresh branch from `origin/master` and port items 1–3 onto `maskIds`, then decide on item 4. For item 4, either you and Anthony agree to replace his flow with mark → Done, or we drop it and keep his. Items 1–3 are small to port, and they're the part of #72 nobody else has done.

The other route is to rebase this branch and resolve every conflict by hand, which means rewriting most of it onto `maskIds` anyway.

Nothing has changed locally: the fetch only updated `origin/master`, and your branch and commits are untouched. Which way do you want to go, and do you want to keep the mark → Done flow or #74's?

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>

```typescript
import React from "react";

import { CaptureUpdateAction } from "@excalidraw/element";

import { Excalidraw } from "../index";

import { API } from "./helpers/api";
import { Pointer } from "./helpers/ui";
import { GlobalTestState, render, unmountComponent } from "./test-utils";

const { h } = window;

const mouse = new Pointer("mouse");

const createMask = (x: number, y: number, maskEnabled = true) => ({
  ...API.createElement({
    type: "ellipse",
    x,
    y,
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    backgroundColor: "#a5d8ff",
    fillStyle: "solid",
  }),
  maskEnabled,
});

/**
 * mask: filled ellipse at (0, 0)–(100, 100)
 * target: filled rectangle at (50, 50)–(150, 150), clipped by the mask, so
 * its bottom-right corner (e.g. (140, 140)) is hidden
 */
const setup = (maskEnabled = true) => {
  const mask = createMask(0, 0, maskEnabled);
  const target = {
    ...API.createElement({
      type: "rectangle",
      x: 50,
      y: 50,
      width: 100,
      height: 100,
      backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
      fillStyle: "solid",
    }),
    maskIds: [mask.id],
  };
  API.updateScene({
    elements: [mask, target],
    captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
  });
  return { mask, target };
};

/** the element clicks and hovers would hit (private, hence the cast) */
const elementAt = (x: number, y: number) =>
  (h.app as any).getElementAtPosition(x, y)?.id;

beforeEach(async () => {
  unmountComponent();
  mouse.reset();
  await render(<Excalidraw autoFocus={true} handleKeyboardGlobally={true} />);
  Object.assign(document, {
    elementFromPoint: () => GlobalTestState.canvas,
  });
});

describe("clicking a masked element", () => {
  it("selects it where it's visible", () => {
    const { target } = setup();

    mouse.clickAt(75, 75);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [target.id]: true });
  });

  it("ignores the parts the mask hides", () => {
    setup();

    mouse.clickAt(140, 140);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({});
  });

  it("can be clicked anywhere while clipping is off", () => {
    const { target } = setup(false);

    mouse.clickAt(140, 140);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [target.id]: true });
  });

  it("only counts the overlap of several masks", () => {
    const first = createMask(0, 0);
    const second = createMask(80, 80);
    // covers both masks; only their small overlap around (90, 90) shows
    const target = {
      ...API.createElement({
        type: "rectangle",
        x: 0,
        y: 0,
        width: 180,
        height: 180,
        backgroundColor: "#ffc9c9",
        fillStyle: "solid",
      }),
      maskIds: [first.id, second.id],
    };
    API.updateScene({
      elements: [first, second, target],
      captureUpdate: CaptureUpdateAction.NEVER,
    });

    expect(elementAt(90, 90)).toBe(target.id);
    // inside the first mask only
    expect(elementAt(30, 50)).not.toBe(target.id);
  });
});

describe("clicking the previewed hidden parts", () => {
  it("selects the element through them while the mask is selected", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();
    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);

    mouse.clickAt(140, 140);

    expect(h.state.selectedElementIds).toEqual({ [target.id]: true });
  });

  it("keeps them hittable while the element or its mask is selected", () => {
    const { mask, target } = setup();

    expect(elementAt(140, 140)).toBe(undefined);

    API.setSelectedElements([target]);
    expect(elementAt(140, 140)).toBe(target.id);

    API.setSelectedElements([mask]);
    expect(elementAt(140, 140)).toBe(target.id);
  });
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-29 20:38:28Z)**_

Very little is lost, and it's all from the masking-mode workflow. Everything users can see on the canvas is kept.

**Kept** (from #74 or the port):

- Images can be masked (ported).
- One mask clips several elements (#74).
- Add elements in the mask's options (#74's own button).
- Ctrl+Alt+G and Remove mask release every child of that mask (#74).
- Adding elements doesn't flip the Clipping switch. #74 only turns clipping on with the first pick ([actionMask.tsx:187-188](packages/excalidraw/actions/actionMask.tsx#L187-L188)).
- Hidden parts can't be clicked, and can be clicked through the preview (ported, now across several masks).
- PNG and SVG export clipping (#74).

**Lost** (all part of the mark → Done flow):

1. **One undo step for a batch.** In #74 each double-click applies straight away as its own undo step, so masking 3 elements takes 3 undos to reverse.
2. **Trying picks out before applying.** There are no blue "marked" outlines, and double-clicking a picked element again doesn't unmark it. Escape and Cancel only leave masking mode, so whatever you've picked so far stays masked.
3. **Releasing one child from inside masking mode.** You can still do it by selecting the child and pressing Ctrl+Alt+G. In #74 that releases the child from **all** its masks, not just one, which only matters now that an element can have several.
4. **The Done button.** #74 finishes with Escape or a double-click on empty canvas instead. Its hint says "Double-click elements to mask them".

**Gained from #74** (the old branch couldn't do these): an element can be clipped by several masks at once, and masks keep working when grouped, ungrouped, duplicated or pasted.

None of the losses is a bug, just a different way of working. If item 1 or 2 matters to your team later, it can be added on top of #74's model as its own change. I'll report the full suite results when they come in.

<pasted_content id="0366"> Closes #73

## Why

A mask could only show what's inside its outline. The only things you could do with its links were add elements one at a time or remove the mask entirely. The parent-child relationship also wasn't visible: nothing on the canvas told you which mask clipped which element, which mattered more once elements could have several masks. #73 asks for:

- control over whether the inside or the outside of a mask is visible;
- a quick way to link everything to a mask, or unlink everything from it;
- visible parent-child tags;

## What changed

- **Mask mode (data model):** new optional `maskMode: "inside" | "outside"` on elements (`packages/element/src/types.ts`). A missing value means `"inside"`, so existing scenes are unchanged. `restore.ts` keeps valid values and drops anything else.
- **Rendering:**
  - **Canvas:** `clipToMask` adds an outer rect as a second subpath and calls `clip("evenodd")`, so the outline becomes a hole.
  - **SVG:** `getMaskSvgPathData` prepends the same rect, and the clip `<path>` gets `clip-rule="evenodd"`.
  - **Rect size:** `getMaskOuterExtent` sizes the rect from the masked element's bounds, so it covers the content at any rotation without huge coordinates.
  - **Mixed modes:** stacked clips still intersect, so several masks with mixed modes work.
- **Actions** (`actionMask.tsx`):
  - `toggleMaskMode` changes only the mask element, never its content, and can be undone.
  - `maskAll` links every element on the canvas that `canBeMasked` allows.
  - `maskNone` unlinks every element from the mask but keeps the options or masking mode open. This is the difference from **Remove mask**.
- **UI:**
  - New shared `MaskModeToggle` ("Show inside | Show outside").
  - It appears in the mask options toolbar **and** the masking-mode bar, so the mode can be set while first creating the mask.
  - **Mask all** and **Mask none** buttons are in both places too.
- **Parent-child tags:**
  - **Where:** drawn on the interactive canvas only, never exported (`renderMaskTags` in `interactiveScene.ts`, data from `getMaskTags` in `renderer/maskClip.ts`).
  - **Naming:** masks are named "Mask 1", "Mask 2", … in scene order. Their elements are named "Mask 1 Child 1", … also in scene order. Numbers shift as masks and links change.
  - **Several masks:** an element with several masks gets one tag per mask, stacked upwards.
  - **When shown:** while a mask is selected or dragged, during masking mode (even before anything is picked), or when a masked element is selected. When a tagged child also belongs to another mask, that mask's own tag is shown too, so the name can be traced.
  - `maskEditor` was added to `InteractiveCanvasAppState` for this.

## Notes

- `maskTransform.test.tsx` (new):
  - **Mask mode:** the inside default, switching to outside with the content untouched, a no-op when the active mode is clicked again, undo/redo, and restore keeping valid values and dropping invalid ones.
  - **Export:** SVG `evenodd` clip paths, the outer rect covering the content at any angle, and the canvas `clip("evenodd")` call.
  - **Mask all / none:** from the options and from the masking-mode bar, including what they skip and that the editor stays open.
  - **Three masks with mixed modes:** produce nested clip groups.
  - **Transforms:** a move → resize → rotate → mode change → move sequence, checking after each step that the export clip matches the mask's geometry and the content stays the same.
  - **Tags:** naming and numbering, scene-order numbering, one tag per mask, renumbering after a mask is deleted, the mask being picked for, unrelated selections, and outside labels.
  - **While picking:** setting the mode before the first pick.
- Existing mask suites pass unchanged: `mask.test.tsx`, `maskActions.test.tsx`, `maskingMode.test.tsx`, `maskEditor.test.tsx`, `maskGroup.test.tsx`, `maskToolbar.test.tsx`.

## Tech debt

**Encountered**

- Several existing tests (`history`, `scroll`, `linearElementEditor`) are timing-sensitive and fail when the machine is busy. With `--update`, a flaky run writes bad snapshots.
- `InteractiveCanvasAppState` is a hand-maintained subset of `AppState`. Any new state the interactive canvas reads has to be added to it, and to `getRelevantAppStateProps`.

**Introduced**

- Tag numbers aren't stored. They're computed from scene order on every interactive render, so a mask's name changes when an earlier mask is removed or reordered. Users can't rename masks yet.
- The outer rect of an outside clip uses a fixed 50px padding (`OUTER_EXTENT_PADDING`) to cover strokes and bound text. Very thick strokes could in theory poke past it.
- **Mask none** and **Remove mask** overlap. They differ only in whether the editor stays open.
- The new strings (`all`, `none`, `showInside`, `showOutside`, `tagMask`, `tagMaskOutside`, `tagChild`) exist only in `en.json`.
- The mode toggle has no keyboard shortcut and isn't in the command palette.

## Review

```markdown
Closes #72

## Why

Masks couldn't clip images: `mask.ts` still said "images are left to #72". Masked elements could also be clicked anywhere in their full shape, even where the mask hides them, so an invisible part could grab clicks meant for whatever was visible underneath. #72 asks for:

- images inside a mask;
- several elements inside one mask (already delivered by #74, so not repeated here);
- masked content that stays editable.

This branch is built on #74's `maskIds` model. An earlier version used the old single `maskId`. It was started before #74 was merged, so the parts #74 didn't cover were moved onto a fresh branch from master.

## What changed

- **Images can be masked:** `"image"` added to `MASKABLE_TYPES` (`packages/element/src/mask.ts`). Canvas and SVG/PNG export need no image-specific code, because the existing clip wraps whatever the element draws.
- **Hidden parts aren't clickable:**
  - **Where:** a new filter in `getElementsAtPosition` (`App.tsx`), next to the existing frame-clip filter. This covers clicking, hover, dragging and double-clicking.
  - **Geometry:** new `isPointInElementMasks` (`collision.ts`) tests the point against each mask's shape with the existing `isPointInElement` and outline checks.
  - **Several masks:** the point has to be inside **all** enabled masks, matching the rendering, where clips intersect.
  - **Clipping off:** the whole element is clickable again.
- **The faint preview is clickable:**
  - New shared `isMaskPreviewShown(element, masks, selectedElementIds)` in `mask.ts`, used by both the preview in `renderer/maskClip.ts` and the click filter. Hidden parts are clickable exactly when they're drawn faintly.
  - The preview now also shows while the **masked element itself** is selected, not just while one of its masks is. Clicking a faint part selects that element, and its hidden parts stay visible and draggable.

## Notes

- `maskHitTest.test.tsx` (new):
  - **Clicking:** a visible part selects the element, a hidden part selects nothing, and with clipping off the whole element is clickable.
  - **Several masks:** only the overlap of two masks counts as a hit.
  - **Preview:** clicking a faint part while the mask is selected selects the element, and faint parts count as hits while the element or its mask is selected.
- `mask.test.tsx`: images moved into the "can be masked" list. Frames and embeds stay unmaskable.
- `maskActions.test.tsx` and `maskingMode.test.tsx`: two tests used an image as the example of something that can't be masked. They now use a frame and another mask.
- Full suite: 140 files, 2113 passed, 0 failed. Typecheck, lint and Prettier are clean, and no snapshots changed.

## Tech debt

**Encountered**

- This branch was first built before #74 was merged, which meant redoing it on the new model. Fetching master before starting a branch for a shared feature would have caught that.
- The full suite times out on busy machines unless run with `--maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1`. With `--update`, a flaky run deletes snapshots.
- In tests, undo silently skips image elements whose `fileId` is `null`. Test images need a `fileId` for undo/redo to work.
- `getElementAtPosition` is private, so the hit tests reach it through `(h.app as any)`.

**Introduced**

- Only `getElementsAtPosition` respects masks, the same as frame clipping. Box and lasso selection, clicking inside an already-selected element's bounding box, arrow binding, snapping and the selection box all still use the element's full bounds.
- Showing the preview while a masked element is selected changes #70's behaviour, where it only showed while the mask was selected.
- The test for "faint parts are hittable" checks the hit lookup directly, not the drawn pixels.

## Review
```

```text
**PR #119: "feat(editor): add basic shape masking (#70)"**
- **Status:** Merged into `master` from `feat/basic-shape-masking` by AntWill-08. Opened by tuna-fisher. Closes issue #70.

**What changed**
- Masking mode is entered from a toolbar submenu button or Ctrl+Alt+G with a shape selected. Double-clicking another shape then masks it so it only shows inside the first shape's borders.
- Currently limited to two shape-stamp objects.
- Selecting the masking shape shows the clipped parts of the masked shape at lower opacity.
- Either shape's mask button or Ctrl+Alt+G releases the mask.
- Double-clicking the masking shape opens a small panel to toggle the visual effect or break the link between the shapes.

**Why:** Gives more control over visible portions of content, which can be paired with motion playback.

**Tech debt**
- Ctrl+G and Ctrl+Shift+G now ignore presses with Alt held, to free up Ctrl+Alt+G.
- The new mask UI copies the plus-banner and motion-path toolbar styles, so they can drift out of sync.
- The access flag for masking never expires.
- Element lookup scans every element because there's no index.
- The 20% clip preview draws an element twice.

**Issues encountered**
- Conflicting shortcuts fail silently, which forced a group hotkey change.
- `newElementWith` skips `undefined`, so mask removal uses `null` instead.
- `restoreElementWithProperties` needs each new optional field listed as an exception.
- `getTextBindableContainerAtPosition` always returns the selected element, so the double-click code needed its own hit test.

**Notes**
- Multi-shape support and indicators showing who is masking whom should be added soon for user clarity.
- Double-click behavior is sometimes inconsistent, possibly depending on machine load.
- The clip follows the shape's geometric outline, not its stroke.
- `App.tsx` may need a closer look later.
- Masking multiple items is easy to add but was intentionally blocked to avoid overlapping another issue's bounds.

**Review:** Requires review from a teammate, and the author expects a possible merge conflict.
```

Written for: teammates reviewing the #72 PR on GitHub, in the same format as your #70 PR (#119).

**Title:** `feat(editor): mask images and block clicks on masked-out parts (#72)`

```markdown
Closes #72

## What changed

- Images can now be masked, the same way as shapes, arrows, freedraw and text. Export to PNG/SVG clips them too.
- The hidden parts of a masked element can no longer be clicked, hovered or dragged. Only the visible part counts. With several masks on one element, only the overlap of all of them counts, same as how it's drawn.
- With clipping turned off in the mask options, the whole element is clickable again.
- The faint 20% preview of the hidden parts is clickable. Selecting a mask (or the masked element itself) shows the preview, and clicking a faint part selects that element so it can be dragged by it.
- The preview now also shows while the masked element itself is selected, not only while its mask is.

## Why

Masks hid content visually, but the hidden parts still grabbed clicks meant for whatever was underneath, which made masked scenes hard to edit. Images were also the main thing users would want to mask (cropping a picture into a shape), and they were the one type left out.

## Tech debt

- Only the main hit test (`getElementsAtPosition`) respects masks, same as frame clipping. Box/lasso selection, clicking inside an already-selected element's bounding box, arrow binding, snapping and the selection handles all still use the element's full bounds.
- The preview showing while a masked element is selected changes #70's behaviour, where it only showed while the mask was selected.
- The new hit tests reach the private `getElementAtPosition` through `(h.app as any)`.

## Issues encountered

- I branched before #74 was merged, built multiple elements + "Add elements" on the old single `maskId` model, and then #74 landed with `maskIds` and its own version of both. I moved the parts #74 didn't cover onto a new branch from master, so this PR is one commit instead of the original five.
- In tests, undo silently skips image elements whose `fileId` is `null`, so test images need a `fileId` for undo/redo to work.
- The full suite times out on a busy machine unless run with `--maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=1`. With `--update`, a flaky run deletes snapshots.

## Notes

- Several elements in one mask and adding elements to an existing mask come from #74, so they aren't in this PR.
- My first version had a mark → Done flow for masking mode (outline picks, unmark them, apply all as one undo step). I didn't bring it over, so we keep #74's double-click-to-apply flow. It could come back later if we want batched picks.
- New `maskHitTest.test.tsx` covers clicking visible vs hidden parts, clipping off, two overlapping masks, and the clickable preview. Full suite: 140 files, 2113 passed.

## Review

Requires review from a teammate.
```
